messages:
ashley_infra: Heads-up — EU-Central hosted GPU pool just triggered a sustained queue-depth alert (p95 queue depth > 18 for 12m).
ashley_infra: Dash shows a pulsing waveform every ~90s, looks like admission control oscillation not a single burst.
mike_sre: Saw it too. Admission rate limits bounced between normal and full-throttle fallback to reserve models.
mike_sre: Logs show a flurry of short seqlen=512 requests from several customers, KV cache hit rate dropped ~20%.
sam_plat: @ashley_infra can you link the dashboard? I want to see regional routing and recent rollout changes.
ashley_infra: https://dash.internal/redwood/eu-central/pool-queuewave — filter set to last 30m, compare to last 6h.
dash-bot: alert: eu-central-gpu-pool.queue_depth.p95 exceeded threshold (18) — triggered at 2024-05-12T14:32:03Z.
ashley_infra: We rotated a canary yesterday that increased tokenization microbatching. Could be sequence-length distribution shift + slightly lower KV cache priming.
sara_cost: If this persists we'll see a bump in per-token cost due to more small batches and fallback to higher-cost reserved instances. Need quick mitigation.
mike_sre: Short-term mitigation: lower admission burst window for hosted tier B by 30%, enable aggressive prefix cache warming for active customers.
ashley_infra: I pushed a canary to reduce client-side burst allowance for tier B via rate-limit config (rolled back in 2m if no regressions).
ashley_infra: Also toggled KV cache prefetch for top 5 active sessions for 15m — monitoring.
sam_plat: Can we route overflow to eu-west spare capacity instead of fallback to smaller models? That keeps latency but costs more egress. Tradeoff ok?
mike_sre: Routing to eu-west is feasible; we need a quick check on network SNAT headroom and egress budget. Also need to respect data residency flags on some tenants.
sara_cost: Make sure to tag routed requests for billing so we can analyze cost delta. If we do this for >5m we'll need approval for extra burst spend.
ashley_infra: Current plan: 1) tighten tier B admission. 2) warm KV cache aggressively. 3) if queue depth not <12 in 10m, enable eu-west spillover for non-residency tenants. 4) follow-up postmortem.
ashley_infra: Anyone object?
mike_sre: +1, start now. I'll watch the scheduler and eviction logs.
sam_plat: +1. I'll prepare a quick feature flag to revert if routing causes errors.
ashley_infra: update: 5m in, p95 queue depth down from 20 -> 13, KV hit up 8%, admission oscillation reduced but still visible.
dash-bot: trend: kv_cache.hit_rate increased by 8% over 5m window.
ashley_infra: keeping spillover off for now. If we hit sustained p95>15 again we'll enable.
sara_cost: Please capture the traffic sample for cost analysis (include tokens, routing, model variant).
mike_sre: grabbing logs + sample, adding to the incident thread.
ashley_infra: thanks — I'll open a follow-up ticket to tune the admission controller PID and add a dashboard panel for oscillation frequency.
sam_plat: note: consider adding a rollout guard to detect seqlen distribution shifts during canaries. That would've flagged this earlier.
ashley_infra: Agreed. Filing that now.
ashley_infra: closing for now, will update if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
